input: app.use('/support/logs', serveIndexMiddleware, serveIndex('logs', { icons: true, view: 'details' })) // vuln-code-snippet vuln-line accessLogDisclosureChallenge

context.guidance: Require authentication on every route that returns Personal Data, and check on each request that the authenticated Data Principal owns the record or holds a role authorised for it. Do not let an identifier supplied in the path or body decide ownership. Apply the check to every method on the route, because Rule 6(1)(b) requires access to the resources holding Personal Data to be controlled.

value.fix: Remove the public directory listing at '/support/logs'. Access logs contain Personal Data such as IP addresses, user agents, request paths and sometimes tokens or email addresses in query strings, and right now anyone can browse and download them without logging in. If the logs are not needed over HTTP, delete the `app.use('/support/logs', ...)` line along with the matching `app.use('/support/logs/:file', logFileServer())` route. If operators do need it, put authentication and role checks in front of every method on both routes, and serve the files without `serveIndex`. For example: `app.use('/support/logs', security.isAuthorized(), security.isAdmin(), express.static('logs', { index: false, dotfiles: 'deny' }))` (or the equivalent: `security.isAuthorized()` plus a middleware that rejects any request where `security.authenticatedUsers.from(req)?.data.role !== 'admin'` with a 403). The role must be read from the verified JWT on the server, never from a path, query or body value. In `logFileServer`, accept only file names on an allow-list or ones matching a strict pattern like `/^access\.log(\.\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})?$/`, and refuse anything containing '/' or '..'. That way a caller-supplied name can't decide which file is read. Better still, move logs out of the web root and send them to a log tool with its own access control. Mask or drop Personal Data fields like IPs and tokens when logging, and add a test that unauthenticated and non-admin requests to '/support/logs' and '/support/logs/<file>' get 401/403 for GET, HEAD and every other method. I haven't applied or tested this change.
